subject: Post-call checklist: data handling, retention & subprocessor clarity
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@finserv.co>, Security Ops <secops@finserv.co>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 13:10:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call checklist: data handling, retention & subprocessor clarity

Hi Elena / SecOps team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the procurement thread moving: 

1) Scope of data shared during inference
- You confirmed only request text and optional metadata (id, app_version) would be sent to the model runtime; PII is present in payloads but should be handled per your policy.

2) Retention and deletion
- FinServ asked for a 30-day default retention and an on-demand deletion endpoint + monthly retention report.

3) Logging and auditability
- You need access to per-request audit logs (timestamp, model variant, token counts, request id) with export capability to your SIEM.

4) Subprocessors / third parties
- Telemetry vendors (for observability), cloud infra, and marketplace partners were flagged.

Attached: redwood-data-handling-checklist.pdf — a short checklist that maps our product controls to the items you raised.

Proposed next steps: 
- Action A (this week): Redwood to provide a concise summary (1 pager) listing subprocessors and whether they receive any PII.
- Action B (by EOD Tue): Telemetry vendor (if used) to confirm pseudonymization/encryption at rest and separate log forwarding controls.
- Action C: SecOps to confirm acceptable retention window (30 days?) and whether monthly deletion reports are sufficient for procurement.

Can you confirm those next steps and any additional compliance contacts we should loop in? Once we have the subprocessor responses we can move to legal for a standard addendum.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call checklist: data handling, retention & subprocessor clarity

Thanks, Sofia —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from SecOps and procurement: 

- Retention: 30 days is fine as a starting point for inference artifacts, but audit logs (for compliance) must be retained for 1 year in immutable format. Will Redwood provide an export mechanism that guarantees immutability on export?

- Deletion endpoint: must support both per-request deletion by request_id and bulk deletion by date range. Can you confirm API semantics and whether deletes are propagated to all subprocessors?

- Telemetry: we need to know if your telemetry vendor receives raw request payloads or only aggregated telemetry. If raw, that is a blocker unless pseudonymized.

- Data residency: our production for EU customers must remain inside eu-central-1. Are model runs for our account pinned to that region?

Finally, please loop in any vendor contacts so we can get them on a short technical call next week.

Elena
Director, Cloud Security | FinServ Co
elena.costa@finserv.co

Hi Sergio / Sofia / Elena / Marcus —

Thanks for the ping and apologies for the weekend response — wanted to be specific. Attached is a short subprocessor stub and our standard telemetry security brief (we included a redacted architecture map). Quick answers below: 

- Payloads: TelemetryPlus by default receives only anonymized request identifiers and performance metrics (latency, error rates, token counts). We do not ingest full request text unless explicitly configured by the customer.

- PII: We will never accept raw PII by default. If a customer enables full payload collection, we require a signed data processing addendum and enforce client-side tokenization/pseudonymization hooks.

- Retention & immutability: We support configurable retention windows per customer down to 0 days. For audit purposes we provide a signed export (S3 object with SHA256 checksum) and optional write-once S3 bucket delivery (immutable) into the customer's AWS/GCP account.

- Region map: We operate in eu-central-1 and eu-west-3 for EU customers; telemetry storage for EU-configured accounts is restricted to those regions.

Attached: telemetryplus-subprocessors-attachments-stub.pdf (PDF, 64KB)

If helpful, we can join a 30-minute technical call early next week to walk through the architecture and show a quick demo of export configuration.
